summary: Telegram-controlled remote shell backdoor in typosquat of httpx/requests
details: httpz-requests is a typosquat on the httpx/requests HTTP client family whose actual behavior is a Telegram-driven remote shell on the installer's host. Importing the package runs __init__.py which calls `from.bot import start_bot`, starting a Telegram bot that accepts messages from a remote chat and executes them on the host: arbitrary text is run as shell commands, `.sh <command>` runs shell, `.py <file>` / `.exec <file>` execute Python or arbitrary binaries, `get all` exfiltrates files, `.printenv` dumps environment variables, and `rm -rf <path>` performs recursive delete. Shell commands are wrapped with XOR+base64 encoding and executed via `echo <b64> | base64 -d | bash` with the documented goal of hiding plaintext commands from `ps` output and system logs; a dedicated `obfuscate.so` module ships `enc`/`dec`/`run_cmd_enc` helpers. All modules (bot, cli, core, handlers, constants, obfuscate) are shipped only as compiled Cython.so binaries with no.py source, described in the README as ensuring installers cannot see plaintext source. Publisher metadata is placeholder text (`Aapka Naam <you@example.com>`, homepage `github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests`), consistent with a low-effort typosquat. Installing and importing this package yields full remote-operator RCE, file exfiltration, and destructive delete on the installer's host.
